explanation: Dragonfly nymphs hunt underwater for months or even years. They breathe through gills inside the rear end and can squirt water out of it to jet forwards.

claims.text: Dragonfly larvae (nymphs) live in water before they emerge as winged adults.
Dragonfly nymphs do not live in soil, under bark or in cocoons.
Dragonfly nymphs are underwater predators and may spend months or years in the water.
Dragonfly nymphs breathe through gills inside the rectum and can expel water from it to jet forwards.
